title: What programs do you use to make your game?
author: UseYourBloodyBrain
selftext: I’ve been working in Godot so far but am very new to all this, what are some of your favourite ai tools and programs to use for making a game together with ai?

comments.author: Marcon2207
comments.body:
I made a tool that streamlines the process of working on a Godot project with Gemini 2.5 pro in the free tier of Google aistudio (other llms should work as well but I like the quality, rate limits and especially the large context window). It exports your entire project as machine readable context together with a powerful system prompt that is aimed to provide educational step by step instructions and creates quality GDScript code.

I am currently working on an agent mode that will directly implement all of the steps inside of Godot, by copying a single output block.

Check it out here: https://marcengelgamedevelopment.itch.io/godot-ai-suite[Godot AI Suite on itch.io](https://marcengelgamedevelopment.itch.io/godot-ai-suite)

comments.author: Mr-33
comments.body: Have you got a video of this working?

comments.author: MrEktidd
comments.body:
Codex in VSCode, until I hit limits then Gemini CLI in VS Code.

Been working great.

replies.author: MrEktidd
replies.body:
Gemini CLI gives you 1000  free agent requests a day (or 60 a minute). 

Highly recommend.  Codex is paid, and much more limited.

replies.author: shoejunk
replies.body: What are the limits of Codex in VSCode? I just started using it on the plus plan.

replies.author: MrEktidd
replies.body: Im not sure what the limit is, I used it for like 6-8 hours though. Now says to wait til next week when limits reset.

replies.author: shoejunk
replies.body: OK, I haven't hit the limit but seems like it might happen to me at some point. I guess I'll go back to Windsurf if it happens.

comments.author: MattDTO
comments.body: I've been playing around with Love2d

comments.author: shoejunk
comments.body: Currently: trying out Codex in VSCode. Preciously, I was using Windsurf. It’s all html/js/css and I post a new game every week using cloudflare as my server.

replies.author: Over_Value1408
replies.body: Can you tell me what kind of games you’ve made?

replies.author: shoejunk
replies.body: Simple old-school arcade-y games. I have the AI make 3 different games - sometimes I have an idea for it to go off of - sometimes I let it pick a game. Then I choose one of those 3 and spend the week iterating on it. So the latest game is a bullet hell/space invaders type of game. (am I allowed to share? Website is [https://botbuiltarcade.com](https://botbuiltarcade.com) )

replies.author: Over_Value1408
replies.body: That’s really cool! What did you use for the artwork, and which game engine are you using?

replies.author: shoejunk
replies.body: I'm not using a game engine. It's all simple 2d stuff using html with canvas + javascript. Artwork is by ChatGPT because it can do pngs with transparencies.

replies.author: Over_Value1408
replies.body: Wow, you completely broke my prejudice that you *have* to use a game engine. Come to think of it, the Canvas API alone would run smoothly on modern devices without any problems. Now I’m even more curious about your projects! I just followed you!!

replies.author: shoejunk
replies.body: Thanks. Yeah, I have an unhealthy affinity for building games from scratch rather than using game engines, but for simple AI-generated 2D games it’s not hard. LLMs can totally do it on its own. If you want to publish on Steam it gets a little bit trickier.

comments.author: WhereIsWebb
comments.body: Bevy, it's in Rust, no visual editor and it works great with codex or Claude code

comments.author: gametank_ai
comments.body: Keep it lightweight: Godot for core, an AI code buddy for boilerplate, and an AI asset tool for cohesive placeholders→final. We build 2D art tools, so devs can stay in flow without hunting packs. Are you aiming for 2D or 3D right now?
